the combination of MAb C215 and topotecan induces a potentiation of antitumor activity and a marked increase of tumor cell death in vitro and in vivo.

the antiproliterative activity of the topoisomerase inhibitor topotecan is markedly enhanced in EGFR-overexpressing tumor cells when combined with the anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody, C225, both in vitro and in vivo.

the sequential treatment of cancer cells with topotecan (a specific inhibitor of the DNA enzyme topoisomerase 1) followed by anti-epiderma growth factor receptor (EGFR)-blocking MAb C225 (which inhibits the growth factor signaling pathway) induces a supraadditive antitumor effect.

the identification and characterization of the molecular targets of anticancer drugs and the elucidation of the mechanisms of action of these drugs.
the identification of new molecular targets for cancer therapy, and the development of innovative therapeutic strategies based on the combination of cytotoxic drugs and biological response modifiers.

the combination of MAb C 225 and topotecam in a sequential schedule is a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of ovarian, breast, or colon cancer.
